bull.b: AVLAYAH provides clinical and regulatory proof that Denali’s transport vehicle platform can deliver a CNS-penetrant biologic from discovery through approval. This validation may support development of additional therapies across lysosomal storage and neurodegenerative diseases.

More than $1.1 billion of pro forma liquidity gives Denali substantial capacity to fund commercialization, clinical trials, and platform investment without immediate reliance on equity financing. This financial flexibility can support execution through multiple development milestones.

Rapid payer coverage is an important foundation for sustained adoption of AVLAYAH because reimbursement access can reduce barriers for physicians and eligible families. Broadening coverage also strengthens Denali’s emerging commercial capabilities and supports future launches.

bear.b: Denali remains far from durable profitability, with minimal trailing revenue compared with a very large net loss. The company must successfully scale AVLAYAH and advance its pipeline over time for commercial earnings to offset the substantial cost base.

Persistent operating and free-cash-flow outflows indicate that Denali’s research and commercialization model currently consumes substantial capital. Even with significant liquidity, continued burn increases dependence on successful launches, milestones, or future financing.

Denali faces established treatment competition, possible new entrants, and emerging gene-therapy alternatives in its target markets. These forces could limit AVLAYAH adoption, influence reimbursement decisions, and make future pipeline commercialization less predictable.
